questions.prompt: Which describe the image in a plane mirror? Choose all that apply.
options: Can be caught on a screen
questions.explain: Plane mirror images are virtual, so they can't be caught on a screen.

questions.prompt: Adam stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is he from his image?
questions.explain: The image is 2 m behind the mirror, so 2 + 2 = 4 m from Adam.

questions.prompt: Adam walks 0.5 m towards the mirror from 2 m away. Now how far is he from his image?
questions.explain: He is 1.5 m from the mirror, and the image is 1.5 m behind it: 3 m.

questions.prompt: Why is AMBULANCE written in mirror writing on the front of ambulances?
options: So drivers ahead read it correctly in their rear-view mirrors
So it can be read from behind
questions.explain: The mirror laterally inverts the mirror writing back to normal.

questions.prompt: You raise your RIGHT hand in front of a mirror. Your image appears to raise its…
questions.explain: Lateral inversion swaps left and right.

questions.prompt: Which words look EXACTLY the same in a plane mirror? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Only palindromes made of symmetrical letters (A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y) work. B isn't symmetrical left to right.

questions.prompt: Trace the light through a periscope, from the object to your eye.
steps: Light from the object enters the top opening
It reflects off the top mirror at 45°
It reflects off the bottom mirror at 45°
questions.explain: Two parallel mirrors at 45° each turn the light through 90°.

questions.prompt: Hill roads in places like Ooty and Shimla have mirrors at sharp bends. Explain how they improve safety, and suggest one limitation.
questions.modelAnswer: The mirrors reflect light from vehicles coming around the blind bend, so drivers can see oncoming traffic they couldn't see directly and slow down, preventing head-on collisions. (Many are convex mirrors, which show a wider view.) Limitations: they can get dirty, fogged or damaged; distances look different in a convex mirror; drivers might rely on them and not honk or slow down.
rubric: Mirror lets drivers see around the bend by reflection
questions.explain: Criterion D: evaluate a real application of mirrors.
